articles.title: The Celestial Tourist Speaks
articles.summary: Jay Freeman recounts an astronomical observing session near the 1998 winter solstice in Central California, braving a severe cold snap at Fremont Peak. Despite freezing temperatures, he set up his Celestron 14 telescope and successfully observed Einstein's Cross, noting the visibility of the gravitational lensing galaxy CGCG 378-15 through his instrument.

articles.title: SJAA Activities Calendar
articles.summary: The SJAA Activities Calendar outlines a series of events for February and March, including multiple star parties at various locations like Fremont Peak, Houge Park, and Coe Peak. It also lists Observational Astronomy classes and General Meetings for members, often held at Houge Park. Key details like sunset times, moon phases, and important disclaimers regarding unofficial events are provided.

articles.title: Highlights of a Saturday Night Star Party
articles.summary: This article details memorable moments from a Saturday night star party, including impressive astronomical observations of Jupiter's Great Red Spot, the Horsehead Nebula, and the Encke Division. Beyond the celestial sights, the author recounts amusing encounters with local wildlife like foxes and raccoons, alongside humorous human elements and discussions of observing conditions.

articles.title: David North
articles.summary: This article provides a detailed guide for lunar observing during February, highlighting the month's unique advantage of high lunar elevation for exceptional viewing conditions. It outlines specific targets and dates from the 22nd to the 26th, recommending various rilles, craters, and mountain ranges such as Hyginus, Triesnecker, Copernicus, and Palus Epidemarum, with tips for amateur astronomers using telescopes. The author encourages observers to explore these changing lunar features, particularly noting the lack of a full moon this month and the opportunity for outstanding steadiness.

articles.title: Akkana Peck
articles.summary: This article announces February 1999 as the start of Mars' apparition, encouraging observers to begin practicing their "Mars eyes" as the planet rapidly brightens and its disk size increases, ahead of its opposition in two months. It details visible features such as the shrinking north polar cap, Hellas, and Syrtis Major, and suggests using filters for observing orographic clouds. The author also provides tips for successful observation, recommending tools like computer programs or Mars globes to help track the planet's rotation and orientation.

articles.title: Start exercising your "Mars eyes" now
articles.summary: This article serves as an observing guide for February, detailing the visibility and key events for various celestial bodies. It highlights good viewing opportunities for Saturn, Venus, Jupiter, and Mercury, including a close conjunction between Venus and Jupiter, and provides tips for spotting Asteroid Vesta. It also notes Pluto's upcoming orbital crossing on February 11th, marking it as a rare chance to observe it as the eighth planet from the sun.

articles.title: Saturday Night Highlights
articles.summary: The article recounts a Saturday night's astronomical observations, featuring bright Geminid meteors and detailed views of deep-sky objects like M82, M31, and an unusually extensive Merope nebula, despite initial concerns about sky transparency. Observations took place on a surprisingly warm December night, highlighting both celestial phenomena and observing conditions.

articles.title: The Celestial Tourist visits Einstein's Cross
articles.summary: The author recounts a challenging but ultimately successful attempt to visually observe Einstein's Cross, a distant quasar gravitationally lensed by galaxy CGCG 378-15. Despite difficulties with high magnification, locating the target, and atmospheric seeing conditions, the observer perceived an irregular structure at the galaxy's core, confirming the presence of the combined lobes of the cross. The article concludes with a reflection on the immense cosmic distances and timescales involved in such an observation.

articles.title: Astronomical Pocket
articles.summary: The SJAA is selling 'Astronomical Pocket' booklets as a fundraiser for its telescope loaner program. These 1999 pocket-sized calendar/reference guides, priced at $10, are filled with astronomical ephemerides, trivia, and custom SJAA club details including contact information, meeting dates, and star parties.

articles.title: Jane Houston
articles.summary: Jane Houston recounts her journey to becoming a SJAA member in May 1998, initially inspired by an amateur astronomer named Timocharis on AOL's Astronomy Forum. Her connection grew through the online Ephemeris and assisting with a John Dobson talk, leading her to join the club. She was impressed by the welcoming community, the availability of telescopes, well-attended star parties, and the club's newsletter and writing talent.

articles.title: Diaries Still Available
articles.summary: The San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA) announces that Astronomical Pocket Diaries (APDs) are still available for a $10 tax-deductible donation, obtainable at club events or by contacting Mark Taylor. Additionally, the article introduces new co-editors for the 'Ephemeris' newsletter and encourages all members, particularly youth, to submit articles about their astronomical adventures.

articles.title: Morris Jones
articles.summary: This article emphasizes the importance of frequent observing, even on nights with uncertain weather, as 'lucky' observers often create their own opportunities for exceptional viewing. It contrasts a legendary December night with a disappointing January session, reinforcing the unpredictability of conditions. The author also shares a personal regret about selling an old telescope while awaiting a new one, advising against parting with beloved instruments based on advice from 'The Dobsonian Telescope'.

articles.title: Island Universes - Starhopping through the Virgo/Coma Realm of Galaxies
articles.summary: This article provides a detailed star-hopping guide for observing numerous galaxies within the Virgo and Coma clusters, specifically aiding astronomers in locating Messier objects and other deep-sky treasures. It offers step-by-step directions, starting from bright guide stars like Spica, to navigate through dense galactic regions, including the Markarian Chain and prominent individual galaxies. The guide shares personal observations and tips, making it practical for completing the Messier challenge in these rich celestial areas.

articles.title: School Star Parties
articles.summary: The article details a series of "School Star Parties" organized by Jim Van Nuland, summarizing a successful 1998 event at Andersen Elementary and announcing upcoming dates for late January and February. These events, primarily held at schools around San Jose, aim to showcase celestial objects to students and local residents. Volunteers are encouraged to contact Jim Van Nuland for details or to confirm event status.

articles.title: Let's go to the Hop
articles.summary: This article provides an observing guide for deep-sky objects, specifically M98, M99, and M100 in the Coma and Virgo constellations. It also includes an extensive astronomical ephemeris for February 1999, detailing lunar phases, positions and magnitudes for Mercury, Venus, Mars, Jupiter, and Saturn, as well as twilight times and a schedule for the darkest Saturday night.

articles.title: Comet Comments
articles.summary: Don Machholz's "Comet Comments" article provides an update on several comets visible in the Winter Milky Way, including Jager, Harrington-Abell, Linear (1998 M5), and Williams. It details recent discoveries such as C/1998 X1 (ODAS), P/1988 VS24 (LINEAR), C/1998 Y1 (LINEAR), and P/1998 Y2 (Li), noting their faintness and orbital characteristics. The article concludes with statistics on amateur comet discoveries, highlighting July and January as the most productive months.

articles.title: Ephemerides — Epoch 2000, Oh UTC
articles.summary: This document provides detailed ephemerides for four comets: C/1998 M5 (LINEAR), C/1998 P1 (Williams), P/1998 U3 (Jager), and 52P/Harrington-Abell. The tables list celestial coordinates (Right Ascension, Declination), elongation, sky visibility (Morning/Evening), and estimated visual magnitude for these comets from January through early March, all referenced to Epoch 2000 and 0h UTC. This information serves as a guide for observers to locate and track these specific comets.

articles.title: Orbital Elements
articles.summary: This document presents a detailed table of orbital elements for four celestial objects: Williams, LINEAR (M5), Harrington-Abell, and Jager. For each object, it provides key astronomical data such as perihelion date and distance, argument of perihelion, ascending node, inclination, eccentricity, orbital period, epoch, and absolute magnitude. The data includes references to MPEC/MPC publications and is presented as part of an SJAA Ephemeris.

articles.title: Officers and Board of Directors
articles.summary: This document lists the current officers and board of directors for an organization, including their positions (President, VP, Secretary, Treasurer, Director) and contact phone numbers. It serves as a directory for the organization's leadership.

articles.title: Ephemeris Staff
articles.summary: This document provides a contact list for the "Ephemeris Staff," detailing the roles of Editor, Circulation, and Printing. It includes names and corresponding phone numbers for each position and service.

articles.title: Submit
articles.summary: The San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA) encourages its members to submit articles for publication in their newsletter, the Ephemeris. Submissions should be sent via email directly to the editors at ephemeris@whiteoaks.com.

articles.title: Telescope Loaner Program Status
articles.summary: The Telescope Loaner Program is currently active, with all telescopes available for use by any SJAA member. Members interested in borrowing a telescope should contact Mike Koop via email or phone, providing both work and home numbers.

articles.title: Available Scopes
articles.summary: This document lists several telescopes, including Dobsons, a refractor, and a Newtonian, that are immediately available for loan to SJAA members. These scopes are stored at various member's homes. Interested members should contact Mike Koop to arrange a pickup at an SJAA event.

articles.title: Scope Loans
articles.summary: This document lists telescopes that have been recently loaned out, detailing the scope description, borrower, and due date. It informs interested individuals that they will be placed on a waiting list until a desired scope becomes available.

articles.title: Extended Scope Loans
articles.summary: This document lists telescopes with extended loan periods available for borrowing. Prospective borrowers can request a scope, and the organization will coordinate a transfer time with the current holder. The list includes various telescope types and their current borrowers, along with due dates or 'Indefinite' status.

articles.title: Waiting List
articles.summary: This document lists individuals currently borrowing telescopes, including a Solar Scope, an 8" Celestron S/C, and an 8" Dobson. It also includes a request for members to volunteer storage space for one or two telescopes.

articles.title: Periodical Publication Statement
articles.summary: This document is a Periodical Publication Statement for the 'SJAA Ephemeris,' the monthly newsletter of the San Jose Astronomical Association. It specifies that the newsletter is published 12 times a year, from January through December. The statement also provides the association's address and instructions for subscribing or unsubscribing from their mailing list, noting its publication in February 1999.

articles.title: San Jose Astronomical Association Membership Form
articles.summary: This document is a membership form for the San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA), detailing fees for regular and junior memberships, as well as an optional subscription to Sky and Telescope magazine. It provides instructions for submitting the form and payment, along with contact information for the organization's treasurer. The form is dated February 1999.
